subtype: Approach: family meeting with a neutral elder mediator [Action]
passage: Come, sit, beta, and I will tell you how our family avoided a court. I am Disha. When our father's house became a quarrel among us, we agreed to meet at my uncle's home, and we asked Irawati, a family friend everyone respected, to run the meeting. She had us speak in turn, without interruption, each with a cup of tea. Before anyone said what they disagreed on, Irawati asked us to list what we agreed on: that the house mattered to us all, that we would not stop speaking, that Amma's room would stay as it was. The list was longer than I expected. When the disagreements came, they sat on the page next to it, looking small. It took three hours. Nobody won. But we left as one family.

qa.a: They met at Disha's uncle's home.

qa.q: What did Disha feel on seeing the list of agreements?
qa.a: Disha felt surprised and encouraged, because the list was longer than expected.

qa.q: What did Irawati do before the disagreements were raised, and why did it help?
qa.a: Irawati asked everyone to list what they agreed on first, so shared ground was visible before the arguments began.

qa.q: How might Irawati have felt running the meeting?
qa.a: Irawati may have felt trusted but careful, since everyone respected her and depended on her to keep the meeting fair.

grounding: The relatives meet at an uncle's home with a respected family friend facilitating, speak in turn and list agreements before disagreements.
